'''Giovanni Battista Rizza''' (7 February 1924 – 15 October 2018), officially known as '''Giambattista Rizza''',<ref>See the [[#CITEREFPresidenza della Repubblica Italiana1973|list of the recipients of the medal "''Benemeriti della Scuola, della Cultura, dell'Arte''"]] and the [[#{{Harvid|Il Ministro dell'Università e della Ricerca Scientifica e Tecnologica|1999}}|Decreto ministeriale 17 febbraio 1999]] conferring him the title of "[[Professor Emeritus]]".</ref> was an Italian mathematician, working in the fields of [[Several complex variables|complex analysis of several variables]] and in [[differential geometry]]: he is known for his contribution to [[hypercomplex analysis]], notably for extending [[Cauchy's integral theorem]] and [[Cauchy's integral formula]] to complex functions of a [[hypercomplex number|hypercomplex variable]],<ref name="Pomini_motivation">According to the motivation for the award of the "''[[Premio Ottorino Pomini]]''", reported on the {{harvtxt|Bollettino UMI|1954|p=477}}, "Sono particolarmente degni di nota i risultati sui teoremi integrali per le funzioni regolari, sulle estensioni della formula integrale di Cauchy alle funzioni monogene sulle algebre complesse dotate di modulo commutative e sul conseguente sviluppo della relativa teoria, ed infine sulla struttura delle algebre di Clifford" ("Particularly notable results are the ones on the integral theorems for regular functions, the ones on the extension of Cauchy integral formula to complex commutative algebras with modulus, and lastly the ones on the structure of [[Clifford algebras]]").</ref> the theory of [[pluriharmonic function]]s and for the introduction of the now called [[Rizza manifold]]s.

== Biography ==
[[Image:1965 International Algebraic Geometry Symposium.jpg|thumb|The International Symposium on Algebraic Geometry held in Rome in 1965. [[Enrico Bompiani]] talking to Giovanni Battista Rizza and [[Vittorio Dalla Volta]].]]

=== Life and academic career ===
Born in [[Piazza Armerina]], the son of Giovanni and Angioletta Bocciarelli, he graduated from the [[Università degli Studi di Genova]], earning his [[laurea]] degree in 1949 under the direction of [[Enzo Martinelli]].<ref name="mar1">According to {{harvtxt|Martinelli|1994|p=1}}, he was his first [[doctoral student]].</ref> In 1956 he was in [[Rome]] at the [[INdAM]], having been awarded a scholarship for his early research activities.<ref>He, [[Giuseppe Arcidiacono]] and Dario Del Pasqua, were awarded the scholarship without sustaining the "''colloquio''"  ("colloquium" in English translation), an oral exam where the candidate was asked to answer questions posed by a scientific jury, according to {{harvtxt|Roghi|2005|p=46}} who reports also an excerpt of the motivation given by the commission for the awarding of the scholarship to Rizza: "... perché trattasi di giovani di cui è nota l'attività scientifica...", i.e. (English translation): "...because they are young researchers whose scientific activity is known, ...").</ref><ref>{{harvtxt|Roghi|2005|pp=8,29,277}} also states that the scientific commission of the institute in charge in 1956 was still the first one, formed on 23 November 1939: its members were [[Francesco Severi]] (the president), [[Luigi Fantappie]], [[Giulio Krall]], [[Enrico Bompiani]] and [[Mauro Picone]].</ref> A year later, in 1957, he was elected "''discepolo ricercatore''"<ref>"Disciple researcher" (English translation) was the appellation of junior research scientists working at the [[INdAM]]. See {{harv|Roghi|2005}} for further details.</ref> in the same institute.<ref name="GRp50">See {{harv|Roghi|2005|p=50}}.</ref> During the same year,<ref>See {{harv|Roghi|2005|p=50}} and {{harvtxt|Severi|1958|p=III}}</ref> he gave some lectures on topics belonging to the field of [[several complex variables]],<ref>See {{harv|Rizza|1958}}.</ref> later included in the lecture notes {{harv|Severi|1958}}.<ref>{{harvtxt|Roghi|2005|p=50}} also precisely reports the costs carried by the [[INdAM]] to fund this course.</ref> In Rome he also met [[Lucilla Bassotti]], who eventually become his wife. In 1961, he won the competitive examination for the chair of "Geometria analitica con elementi di Geometria Proiettiva e Geometria Descrittiva con Disegno" of the [[University of Parma]],<ref>"[[Analytic geometry]] with elements of [[projective geometry]] and [[descriptive geometry]] with [[drawing]]" (English translation).</ref> scoring first out of the three finalists:<ref>See the announce on the {{harvtxt|Bollettino UMI|1962|p=454}}.</ref> a year later, in 1962, he became [[extraordinary professor]],<ref>See {{harv|Venturini|1963|p=15}}.</ref> and then, in 1965, [[ordinary professor]] to the same chair.<ref>See the [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|1965}}|1965 Yearbook of the University of Parma, p. 207]]: the exact date of this career advancement is 16th January 1965.</ref> In 1979 he became ordinary professor of "''Geometria superiore''",<ref>Literally "higher geometry": it is an Italian university course on advanced geometry topics.</ref> holding that chair uninterruptedly until 1994:<ref>See the [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|1980}}|1980 Yearbook of the University of Parma, p. 209]].</ref> from 1994 up to his retirement in 1997, he was "''professore fuori ruolo''" in the same department of mathematics where he worked for more than 35 years.<ref>See the [[#{{harvid|The Editorial Board|1995}}|1995 Yearbook of the University of Parma, pp. 887 and 1036]]: the locution, literally meaning "out of role professor", identifies a nearly retired professor which is not in charge of any particular university course.</ref>

Apart from his research and teaching work, he was actively involved as a member of the editorial board of the "''[[Rivista di Matematica della Università di Parma]]''", and served also as the journal director from 1992 to 1997.<ref>According to the [[timeline]] of Editors in Chief of the "''Rivista''", as reported in the [[#CITEREF%5B%5BRivista di Matematica della Università di Parma%5D%5D2013|historical section of the journal web site]].</ref>

Rizza died in Parma on 15 October 2018, at the age of 94.<ref>{{cite web |title=Giambattista Rizza |url=https://www.necrologi-italia.it/Parma/funerale-Giambattista-Rizza-22278.php |website=Necrologi Italia |access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=È Scomparsa Lucilla Bassotti Rizza |url=https://www.ing.uniroma1.it/en/archivionotizie/scomparsa-lucilla-bassotti-rizza |website=Università degli Studi di Roma "La Sapienza" |access-date=18 February 2023}}</ref>

=== Honors ===
In 1954 he was awarded the [[Ottorino Pomini prize]] by the [[Unione Matematica Italiana]], jointly with [[Gabriele Darbo]]: the judging commission was composed by [[Giovanni Sansone]] (as the president), [[Alessandro Terracini]], [[Beniamino Segre]], [[Giuseppe Scorza-Dragoni]], [[Carlo Miranda]], [[Mario Villa]] and [[Enzo Martinelli]] (as the secretary).<ref name="Pomini"/>

In 1973 he was awarded the [[golden medal]] "[[Benemeriti della Scuola, della Cultura, dell'Arte]]" by the [[President of the Italian Republic]],<ref name="Ben"/> as an acknowledgement his research and teaching and achievements as civil servant at the University of Parma.<ref>See {{harv|Schreiber|1973|p=1}}.</ref>

In 1995, to celebrate his 70th birthday, an international conference on differential geometry was organized in Parma: the [[proceedings]] were later published as a special issue of the "Rivista di Matematica della Università di Parma".<ref>See {{harv|Donnini|Gigante|Mangione|1994}}. In the [[preface]], the editors and members of the organizing committee briefly commemorate [[Franco Tricerri]], former pupil of Rizza and speaker at the conference, who died in a [[plane crash]] in [[China]] few weeks before the proceedings of the conference were published (<!-- ''[[ibid.]]'', -->[[#{{harvid|Donnini|Gigante|Mangione|1994}}|p. iii]]).</ref>
In 1999 the University of Parma, where he worked for more than 35 years, awarded him the title of [[professor emeritus]].<ref>According to [[#{{Harvid|Il Ministro dell'Università e della Ricerca Scientifica e Tecnologica|1999}}|Decreto ministeriale 17 febbraio 1999]].</ref>

Rizza was an honorary member of the [[Balkan Society of Geometers]] and life member of the [[Tensor Society]].<ref>See the list of members of the {{harvtxt|Balkan Society of Geometers|2011}} and of the {{harvtxt|Tensor Society|2010}}.</ref>

=== Personality traits ===
[[Enzo Martinelli]] described Giovanni Battista Rizza as a passionate researcher with a "strong intellectual force",<ref name="Marp1">{{harvtxt|Martinelli|1994|p=1}} precisely characterizes Rizza's scientific work as developed with "''...molta passione e forza intellettuale...''", i.e. with (English translation) "...much passion and intellectual force...".</ref> and his scientific work as rich of [[Geometry|geometrical]] ideas, denoting his strong [[algorithm]]ic ability.<ref>Again according to {{harvtxt|Martinelli|1994|p=2}}: "Queste poche righe mi auguro siano servite a dimostrare che Rizza è un matematico ricco di idee geometriche e dotato di forti capacità algoritmiche.", i.e. (free English translation) "I hope those few lines have been of some help in demonstrating that Rizza is a mathematician rich of geometrical ideas and gifted with a strong algorithmic ability."</ref> According to Martinelli, Rizza is also a skilled organizer:<ref name="Marp2">See {{harv|Martinelli|1994|p=2}}.</ref> his ability in organizational tasks is also acknowledged and praised by {{harvtxt|Schreiber|1973|p=1}}, who also alludes the positive opinions of colleagues and students alike about his involvement in research, teaching and administrative duties at the mathematics department of the [[University of Parma]].

== Work ==

=== Research activity ===
Giovanni Battista Rizza authored 53 research papers and 30 other scientific works, including research announcements, short notes, surveys and reports: he also wrote didactic notes and papers on historical topics, including commemorations of other scientists.<ref>See, for example, {{harv|Rizza|1984}}, {{harv|Rizza|1986}} and {{harv|Rizza|2002}}.</ref> His main fields of research were the [[Hypercomplex analysis|theory of functions on algebras]], the [[Several complex variables|theory of functions of several complex variables]], and [[differential geometry]].

==== Theory of functions on algebras ====
The theory of functions on algebras, also referred to as [[hypercomplex analysis]], is the study of [[Function (mathematics)|function]]s whose [[Domain of a function|domain]] is a [[subset]] of an [[algebra over a field|algebra]].<ref>For more information see the survey article by {{harvtxt|Rizza|1973}} and the references cited therein.</ref> The first works of Giovanni Battista Rizza belong to this field of research, and he was awarded the [[Premio Ottorino Pomini]] for his contributions.<ref name="Pomini_motivation" />

His first main result is the extension of [[Cauchy's integral theorem]] to every [[monogenic function]] {{math|F}} on a general [[algebra over a field|complex algebra]] {{math|'''''A'''''}},<ref>See {{harv|Rizza|1950}}.</ref>
: <math>\int_{\Gamma_1} \mathrm{F}(\mathrm{X}) \mathrm{d}\mathrm{X}=0</math>
where {{math|Γ{{sub|1}}}} is a [[Cycle (algebraic topology)|1-dimensional cycle]] homologous to zero, and also satisfying other technical conditions.

Few years later, he extended [[Cauchy's integral formula]] to every [[monogenic function]] {{math|F}} on a [[Commutative algebra (structure)|commutative]] [[Normed algebra|normed]] [[algebra over a field|real algebra]] {{math|'''''A'''''{{sup|*}}}},<ref>See {{harv|Rizza|1952}}, {{harv|Rizza|1952a}} and the survey {{harv|Rizza|1973}}.</ref> [[Isomorphism (algebra)|isomorphic]] to a given complex algebra {{math|'''''A'''''}}:<ref>In the terminology of {{harvs|txt|first=|last=Rizza|author1-link=|year=1952|year2=1952a}}, the algebra {{math|'''''A'''''{{sup|*}}}} is said to be the ''real image of''  (precisely, ''l'immagine reale di'') {{math|'''''A'''''}}.</ref> precisely, he proves the formula
: <math>\int_{\Gamma_1}\frac{\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{X})}{\mathrm{X}-\Xi}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{X}=2\pi i\sum^k_{s=1}\mathrm{N}^{(s)}u^{(s)}\mathrm{F}(\Xi)</math>
where
* {{math|X&nbsp;≡&nbsp;''x''{{sup|*}}&nbsp;≡&nbsp;''x''}} identifies indifferently a [[Point (mathematics)|point]] in the complex algebra {{math|'''''A'''''}} or in its isomorphic real algebra {{math|'''''A'''''{{sup|*}}}},
* {{math|Γ{{sub|1}}}} is again a [[Cycle (algebraic topology)|1-dimensional cycle]] homologous to zero, and satisfying other technical conditions,
* {{math|N{{sup|(''s'')}}}} is the [[winding number]] of the cycle {{math|Γ{{sub|1}}}} respect to the [[zero divisor]] [[Locus (mathematics)|locus]] for the considered algebra.

==== Theory of analytic functions of several complex variables ====

{{quote
|text= All'estensione, tutt'altro che banale, allo spazio {{math|''R''{{I sup|2''n''}}}} dei metodi di Martinelli per dimostrare la {{EquationNote|1|(3)}}, è dedicata una Memoria [[#{{harvid|Rizza|1955}}|[8]]] di Giovanni Battista Rizza, il quale, sempre nell'ipotesi {{math|''ρ''(''x''{{sub|1}},&nbsp;''y''{{sub|1}},...,&nbsp;''x{{sub|n}}'',&nbsp;''y{{sub|n}}'')&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''C''{{I sup|ω}}}}, perviene a stabilire la {{EquationNote|1|(3)}} per {{math|''n''}} qualsiasi. Anche questo lavoro, per quanto redatto in lingua inglese e pubblicato su una delle principali riviste matematiche, non ha nella letteratura attuale, la notorietà che meriterebbe.<ref>(English translation): "To the far from trivial extension to the {{math|''R''{{I sup|2n}}}} space of Martinelli's methods in order to prove (3) a Memoir [8] of Giovanni Battista Rizza is devoted, who, again under the hypothesis that {{math|''ρ''(''x''{{sub|1}},&nbsp;''y''{{sub|1}},...,&nbsp;''x''{{sub|n}},&nbsp;''y''{{sub|n}})&nbsp;∈&nbsp;''C''{{I sup|ω}}}}, succeeds in proving (3) for every {{math|''n''}}. Even this work, despite being written in English and published in a major mathematical journal, has not, in the current literature, the notoriety it deserves".</ref>
|sign= [[Gaetano Fichera]]
|source= {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=135}}.
}}

Rizza published only three work in this field:<ref>The work {{harv|Rizza|1954}} is only a research announcement related to the {{harv|Rizza|1955}}, while {{harv|Rizza|1958}} is set of course notes based on the same paper and on {{harv|Rizza|1957}}.</ref> in the first one, the highly remarkable memoir {{harv|Rizza|1955}},<ref>According to {{harvtxt|Fichera|1982b|p=24}}, who praises this work as "''molto considerevole''": see also his comments in {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=135}}.</ref> he extends to pluriharmonic functions of {{math|2''n''}} [[Function of a real variable|real variables]], {{math|''n''&nbsp;>&nbsp;2}}, the methods introduced by Enzo Martinelli in order to give new proof of a result of [[Luigi Amoroso]] for pluriharmonic functions of four real variables.<ref>See {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=135}}, {{harv|Fichera|1982b|pp=24–25}} and {{harv|Martinelli|1941}}.</ref> Precisely, he proves the following formula

{{NumBlk|::::::::::::::::::::|<math>\frac{\partial u}{\partial \nu} = \frac{\vert\nabla \rho\vert^3}{Q(\rho)} E u</math>|{{EquationRef|1}}}}
where
* {{math|''u''}} is a polyharmonic function defined on a [[Bounded set|bounded]] [[Domain (mathematical analysis)|domain]] {{math|Ω}},
* {{math|''ρ''}} is a [[Real number|real]] [[analytic function]] defining the [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] of {{math|Ω}} by the equation
: <math>\partial\Omega = \{x\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}|\rho(x)=0\},</math>
* {{math|''Q''(''ρ'')}} is a linear combination of the [[CR manifold#The Levi form|Levi forms]] of {{math|''ρ''}} relative to couples of [[complex variable]]s,
* {{math|''E''}} is a linear [[tangential operator]] defined on {{math|∂Ω}}.
Formula {{EquationNote|1|(1)}} express a condition the [[normal derivative]] of the boundary value of a pluriharmonic function on domain with real analytic boundary must satisfy.<ref>See {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=135}}, {{harv|Fichera|1982b|pp=24–25}} and {{harv|Fuks|1963|loc=p. 277, footnote 1}}.</ref> It can be used to construct an integral representation for pluriharmonic functions on such kind of domains, by using the [[Green's identities#Green's third identity|Green's formula]] for the [[Laplacian]],<ref>See {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=134}}, {{harv|Fichera|1982b|p=33}} and {{harv|Martinelli|1941|p=162}}.</ref> and also to establish an [[integro-differential equation]] boundary values of pluriharmonic functions must satisfy.<ref>It is the [[Amoroso integro-differential equation]]: see {{harv|Fichera|1982a|p=134}} and {{harv|Fichera|1982b|pp=33}}.</ref> Rizza's result motivated other works on the same topic by Gaetano Fichera, Paolo de Bartolomeis and [[Giuseppe Tomassini]].<ref>See the hystorical survey sections in {{harv|Fichera|1982b|p=25}} and the work {{harv|de Bartolomeis|Tomassini|1981|p=33}}.</ref>

"Materials toward a history of the Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica from 1939 to 2003" (English translation of title) is a [[monograph]]ic [[Serial (literature)|fascicle]] published on the "Bollettino della Unione Matematica Italiana", describing the history of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi]] from its foundation in 1939 to 2003. It was written by [[Gino Roghi]] and includes a presentation by Salvatore Coen and a preface by [[Corrado De Concini]]. It is almost exclusively based on [[source text|sources]] from the institute archives: the wealth and variety of materials included, jointly with its [[Addendum#In books|appendices]] and [[Index (publishing)|indexes]], make this monograph a useful reference not only for the history of the [[institute]] itself, but also for the history of many [[mathematician]]s who taught, followed the institute courses or simply worked there.
